title: Mastery of the Tensilon (Edrophonium) Test
summary: The Tensilon test is a diagnostic procedure historically used to confirm Myasthenia Gravis (MG) by temporarily improving neuromuscular transmission. While largely superseded by serological and electrodiagnostic testing, understanding its execution and interpretation remains essential for every ophthalmologist.

sections.title: Definition & Mechanism
sections.content: Edrophonium chloride is a rapid-acting, short-lived acetylcholinesterase inhibitor. It prevents the degradation of acetylcholine (ACh) in the synaptic cleft, increasing the probability of binding to postsynaptic nicotinic ACh receptors. In patients with MG, this transiently overcomes the blockade caused by autoantibodies, resulting in objective improvement of ptosis or extraocular muscle (EOM) function.

sections.title: Safety Protocols (RED FLAGS)
content: Atropine sulfate (0.5–1.0 mg) MUST be at the bedside in a syringe to counteract cholinergic crisis/bradycardia.
Cardiac monitoring and pulse oximetry are mandatory during the procedure.
Contraindicated in patients with asthma, COPD, and high-degree AV block.
The test is considered 'positive' only if an objective, quantifiable improvement (e.g., ptosis reversal) is observed.

sections.title: Procedure Protocol
content: Step 1: Baseline measurement of ptosis (palpebral fissure height) and EOM motility.
Step 2: Administer 2 mg IV over 15-30 seconds as a test dose.
Step 3: Wait 60 seconds. Monitor for side effects (fasciculations, bradycardia).
Step 4: If no side effects, administer the remaining 8 mg IV.
Step 5: Observe and record maximal improvement within 2-5 minutes of injection.

content.explanation: Salivation, Lacrimation, Urination, Defecation, Gastric upset, Emesis (Muscarinic effects of cholinergic excess).

sections.title: Clinical Pearls
content: The test is highly sensitive for ocular MG but has low specificity (false positives in ALS, Eaton-Lambert, and brainstem lesions).
Place a cold pack over the ptotic eyelid for 2 minutes (Ice Pack Test) as a safe, non-pharmacological alternative.
Always document the objective measurement (e.g., 'Ptosis improved from 2mm to 7mm').
Sensitivity decreases as the duration of MG increases.
